method: Five consecutive actual JPEG rows, from one row before the first captured phase13/14 through three rows after, restricted to the same case. Existing crop rectangle and label placement reused. No source pixel modification beyond cropping; no retiming or fabricated frames.
general_visual_observations: Head and low reticles/tracers meet the corresponding visible anatomical areas in all six variants. Cyan live-hit markers distinguish surviving pistol/rifle targets from the yellow markers in these lethal shotgun cases.

Player and target silhouettes remain distinct. Blood remains local and restrained in the selected windows. Pale base, violet Last Word, cyan Overcurrent and warm orange Gravebreaker tracers remain identifiable.

No obvious bent tracer, newly displaced blood burst, full-screen flash or stretched-limb geometry was identified in these selected images. Some red specks above the player predate the sampled shotgun shots and were not counted as their fresh impact effects.
Later crowd originals show locally folded bodies: one for Remington 870, two for Gravebreaker. The surviving targets remain upright.

limitations: This is a smaller confirmatory S3 review, separate from the earlier S1 review. Every one of these 14 sheets and four full originals was actually opened. No earlier frame or observation is relabelled as S3 evidence.

Five consecutive JPEG rows per case cover roughly 0.13-0.17 seconds, not complete encounters. Two later crowd originals add aftermath context. Complete head/limb separation paths, settled ragdoll behavior over time and untested close/wounded-head cases are outside this review.

Sheets contain only an unscaled crop at [710,335,1320,655] with labels outside source pixels. Four full 1600x900 originals confirm context. All original captures are JPEG; no source image is modified.

Labels are assigned at asynchronous screenshot callback time. A row preceding phase13/14 can already contain a fired tracer, so the selection does not guarantee a pre-shot image for every case. Audio seconds are a CPU capture clock; exact render/audio synchronization is not measured.

The arranged targets use the explicit standing-pose fixture. This does not establish natural enemy pursuit/attack behavior or whole-match accumulation. A persistent HUD gain value can belong to a previous case.
No continuous playback, audio audition, native controls, performance measurement or user approval of the visual direction is claimed. Pickup-symbol review is separate.
